about: discord's decision table (the P3 procedure: demand, then this table, then the code): each operation the pack serves, the demand it answers (journeys/demand.json, the life's seeding through the vendor's own API, or a refresh scope of the manifest) and the mechanism that serves it. Every Discord route the demand reaches is permission-checked, so each is a handler; every other operation of the spec is `unmodeled` (the manifest) and answers the vendor's gap, the operations only an opt-in provider of a third-party application calls (demand.json's `optional`) among them. The Gateway is the manifest's socket (the kernel's sockets.ts), spoken by semantics/sockets.ts; the authorize page is the manifest's screen.

decisions.demand: No scanned application calls it; the customer life walks it.
decisions.why: an action: a code or a refresh token spent once, a token pair issued (drawn from the World's secret, kept by SHA-256); a bot install's answer carries the guild; the client credentials grant answers the gap (no demand, no life step)

decisions.demand: No scanned application calls it; the customer life walks it.
decisions.why: a computed read: the bearer token's application, scopes, expiry and user

decisions.demand: Volter Harness reads its application's id and verify_key (the Chat SDK's Discord adapter needs both, Hermes's env carries neither); the vendor-backed refresh reads application back (the manifest's refresh of application); the life's helper bot reads its own application as it starts
decisions.why: a computed read: the Bot token's application, with its server count

decisions.demand: the vendor-backed refresh reads guild back (the manifest's refresh of guild); the life's helper bot lists its servers as it starts
decisions.why: a computed read: the caller's memberships, each guild partial with the caller's permissions (counts when asked)

decisions.demand: No scanned application calls it; the customer life walks it.
decisions.why: a computed read: the server's channels without threads (from 2026-11-16 the ones the bot cannot view omitted)

decisions.demand: the life builds the server's channels through the vendor's own API (the seeding rule): #classes, #bookings, #announcements and a private #teachers
decisions.why: an action under MANAGE_CHANNELS, overwrites bounded by the bot's own permissions

decisions.demand: the life makes the server's roles through the vendor's own API (the seeding rule)
decisions.why: an action under MANAGE_ROLES: a role placed at the bottom, the others moved up

decisions.demand: No scanned application calls it; the customer life walks it.
decisions.why: a read by a member, by position

decisions.demand: No scanned application calls it; the customer life walks it.
decisions.why: a computed read: username, global name or nickname prefix, limit 1-1000

decisions.demand: No scanned application calls it; the customer life walks it.
decisions.why: an update under CHANGE_NICKNAME, a bot only

decisions.demand: Hermes (Open Autonomy) answers in the thread it opened and posts its report to its home channel; Volter Harness's agent replies in a thread and posts to its home channel by its bare id; the life's helper bot answers a question as a reply
decisions.why: an action: permissions, content rules, attachments, mentions; MESSAGE_CREATE on the Gateway

decisions.demand: Hermes (Open Autonomy) and Volter Harness's Chat SDK adapter each open one on a message that mentions the bot
decisions.why: an action: a thread whose id is the message's, once (160004)

decisions.demand: the life makes Cal.com's webhook in #bookings through the vendor's own API (the seeding rule: the helper bot makes it, as a person makes one in the channel's Integrations)
decisions.why: an action under MANAGE_WEBHOOKS; the token drawn from the World's secret, kept by SHA-256

decisions.demand: Cal.com posts its booking template to a Discord webhook URL; Hermes sends interaction followups
decisions.why: an action: the webhook's message, 204, or the message with wait=true; an interaction token always returns a message and completes a first deferred response

decisions.demand: the life makes the invite people join the server by through the vendor's own API (the seeding rule): the helper bot asks for the studio's invite each time it starts
decisions.why: an action under CREATE_INSTANT_INVITE, a similar open invite reused unless unique

decisions.demand: Volter Harness's discord.js finds the Gateway; the platform's own callers: a World finds the vendor's socket where its API says it is (twin-world's architecture, sockets); the life's helper bot finds the Gateway
decisions.why: a computed read: the twin's own socket URL and the bot's session start limit, counted from its identifies

decisions.demand: the vendor-backed refresh reads message back (the manifest's refresh of message, per channel)
decisions.why: a computed read under VIEW_CHANNEL: a channel's messages newest first, paged by before, after or around; none without READ_MESSAGE_HISTORY

decisions.demand: the vendor-backed refresh reads webhook back (the manifest's refresh of webhook, per guild)
decisions.why: a read under MANAGE_WEBHOOKS: the server's webhooks with their creators and an incoming webhook's token

decisions.demand: the vendor-backed refresh reads invite back (the manifest's refresh of invite, per guild)
decisions.why: a read under MANAGE_GUILD or VIEW_AUDIT_LOG: the server's live invites, their metadata only under MANAGE_GUILD

decisions.demand: Open Autonomy's setup checks the bot's application against the project's branding (name, id); Hermes's discord.py reads it as it logs in (its owner and flags)
decisions.why: a computed read: the Bot token's application, with its owner and bot

decisions.demand: Hermes's discord.py logs in by reading the bot's own user
decisions.why: one resource's views: the caller itself, email only under the email scope

decisions.demand: Open Autonomy's setup checks the home channel is a server channel; Hermes reads a channel it has not cached before posting to it
decisions.why: a read under VIEW_CHANNEL (50001 without it, 10003 for none)

decisions.demand: Hermes shows it is typing while its agent answers
decisions.why: an acknowledgement under VIEW_CHANNEL: 204, nothing stored (the indicator lasts ten seconds)

decisions.demand: Hermes edits its progress message in place as its agent works, then to the answer
decisions.why: an update by the author only (50005); MESSAGE_UPDATE on the Gateway

decisions.demand: Hermes marks a message it is answering with 👀, and with ✅ or ❌ when its turn ends
decisions.why: a set member: one subject per message, emoji and user (10014 for an emoji the World does not have, ADD_REACTIONS unless someone already reacted with it); MESSAGE_REACTION_ADD on the Gateway

decisions.demand: Hermes takes back its 👀 when its turn ends
decisions.why: a set member removed (204 whether or not it was there); MESSAGE_REACTION_REMOVE on the Gateway

decisions.demand: Hermes's slash-command sync, on by default (DISCORD_COMMAND_SYNC_POLICY "safe"), lists the application's global commands on every start to diff them against its own (discord.py's tree.fetch_commands); the vendor-backed refresh reads command back (the manifest's refresh of command)
decisions.why: a computed read by the application's own bot: its live global commands, the localization dictionaries only when with_localizations asks

decisions.demand: Hermes's sync creates each of its commands the application lacks (discord.py's upsert_global_command); Aaron's scratch script registers /ping and /status the morning before (the life)
decisions.why: an action: a chat-input command checked as the page states (name, description, options, choices, required first, 100 a scope), stored as Discord answers it with a new version; a name already used overwrites that command (200); the other command types answer the gap

decisions.demand: Hermes's sync edits a command whose name, description or options differ from its own (discord.py's edit_global_command): /status as Aaron's script left it
decisions.why: an action: the fields given overwrite the command's, checked as a create's, a new version; a name another command holds is refused (40041)

decisions.demand: Hermes's sync deletes the commands it no longer has, before creating any (discord.py's delete_global_command): /ping
decisions.why: an action: the command removed (204); one the application does not have is 10063

decisions.demand: Hermes's slash commands (an ephemeral defer, or the authorization refusal) and its confirmation buttons (the prompt updated in place)
decisions.why: A token-authenticated single initial response within three seconds: a command message or a defer, a component's update or deferred update, and /skill's autocomplete; with_response answers the callback object. Other interaction flows answer the gap.

decisions.demand: Hermes's slash commands that acknowledge (/status: Status sent~) edit the deferred response
decisions.why: The interaction token edits its own original message for fifteen minutes, completing a deferred response and keeping its ephemeral state.

decisions.demand: Hermes's slash commands with no acknowledgement (/usage, /reload-mcp) delete the deferred response
decisions.why: The token removes its original interaction response (204), an empty deferred response included.

decisions.demand: Twenty's website shows its Discord community's member count by reading its invite (twentyhq/twenty 1d561b8c73c9 packages/twenty-website, demand.json)
decisions.why: A computed read: the invite's public view (no uses, limits or creation) and, with with_counts, the guild's approximate member and online counts.

decisions.demand: a person invokes a command, autocomplete or a component in the client, which no API call does (the life's interactions)
decisions.why: Discord's client sends an interaction from a person's act; the door is that act.

decisions.demand: a World's application takes its Discord app credentials from the World
decisions.why: The Developer Portal makes an application and its bot token on its pages; no API call makes one.

decisions.demand: the people of the life, who sign up in Discord's client
decisions.why: Discord's API makes no account; a person registers in the client.

decisions.demand: a person creates a server in the client
decisions.why: A user creates a guild in the client (bots may not), with @everyone, #general and General.

decisions.demand: a person accepts an invite in the client
decisions.why: Joining through an invite is the client's act on the person's session, not an API call a bot makes.

decisions.demand: a person posts a message in the client
decisions.why: A person's message is sent by the client on their session; the API's message create is a bot's.

decisions.demand: a person reacts to a message in the client
decisions.why: A person's reaction is the client's act on their session.
